correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the drift and first-exit argument in RESULT.md:32–62. Both branches give the same linear increment μ+α|x| for x+y; the quadratic correction gives the exact additional term λ[y²−(−δx+E₂)²]. On the ball, Q=x²+y²+μ² and s=|x|+|y|+μ satisfy s²≤3Q and s≤3η. Thus the cost from the remainder sum is at most 6CQ, and λ(−δx+E₂)²≤2λD²x²+54λC²η²Q. The radius conditions leave at least μ/2+α|x|/2+(6C+1)y² of drift, on the switch as well. These conditions admit a positive radius including C=0. The bound |Φ|≤K yields a contradiction if all iterates through floor(4K/μ)+1 stay in the closed ball; only updates from inside are needed. The proof uses no sign restrictions on δL,δR and no smoothness beyond the stated remainder hypotheses. The inspected verify.py is a supplementary finite exact-fraction test of the weaker drift μ/2 for one remainder pair and four determinant-sign patterns; it was not executed and is not needed for the proof.

value.rationale: A motivated partial resolution of an explicit nonlinear nonsmooth-fold question: at a fixed local radius the same quantitative O(μ⁻¹) exit estimate works over both branches and an infinite family of remainders, including parameter-dependent cross terms. The quadratic gauge handles a genuine breakdown of the linear drift near the switch. This is not a claim about higher dimensions, arbitrary first-order-small errors, or global divergence.
